paper_metadata.title: Effects of Ge addition on the structure, mechanical and magnetic properties of (CoCrFeNi)100-xGex high-entropy alloys

evidence.quote: The microstructure, mechanical and magnetic properties of (CoCrFeNi)100-xGex (molar ratio, x= 0 ∼ 33) high-entropy alloys (HEAs) have been systematically studied in this paper.

attributes.morphology: fine precipitated phase along grain boundaries

evidence.quote: G25 alloy is not a pure single BCC phase. The fine precipitated phase structure appears along the grain boundaries. It can also be observed from the EBSD phase distribution diagram(as shown in figure 5(h)) that the precipitated phase is a hexagonal intermetallic compound.

When x increases to 33, it is conﬁrmed that there is a single phase in the alloy. All the diffraction peaks can be indexed with a hexagonal structure, and the lattice parameters of a and c are 4.092(1) Å and 5.145(2) Å, respectively.
Analysis combined with EBSD results shown in ﬁgures 5(a), (b) and (e), (f) conﬁrms the presence of equiaxed FCC grains in these alloys.

attributes.composition: Ge ∼25 at% in ID, ∼10 at% in DR

evidence.quote: The bright regions contain more Ge than the dark regions. The atomic percentage of Ge in ID region is greater than that of other metal elements(∼25 at%), while the atomic percentage of germanium in DR region is only half of that of other metal elements(∼10 at%). The higher concentrations of Ge element were detected in the segregation region.
With the increase of hardness, the sample also became more brittle. As can be seen inﬁgure 4(h), the appearance of many cracks was caused by the increase of brittleness.

conditions.test_method: VSM, magnetic field up to 7 T

evidence.quote: With the increase of BCC phase volume fraction in Ge25 alloy, the coercivity(Mc) value decreases to 28.5 Oe and the saturation(Ms) magnetization increases to 46.1 emu/g(as shown inﬁgure 7).
We believe that the improved YS and UTS is mainly due to the addition Ge which enhanced by solid solution strengthening.
When Ge is added to the solid solution(CoCrFeNi)100-xGex, the lattice is further distorted which prohibits the motion of dislocation and may result in further increase of strength.
The hysteresis loop in the M-H curve ofﬁgure 7 associated with the paramagnetic to ferromagnetic transition is due to the formation of the BCC phase(x > 10).
